description: Found in defk-52v.15 and confirmed by defk-tif (examples/cdcl_sat.exs notes). A nested loop whose range or initial value reads the array that the loop body then writes and returns (e.g. for k <- 0..(st[@h_n] - 1)//1, reduce: st do ... st[k] = ... end, or an inner reduce_while init that reads st) copies st, because the range/init read counts as a read after the write. Workaround today: read the bound into a local first (n = st[@h_n]; for k <- 0..(n - 1)//1, ...). The range and init are evaluated once before the loop runs, so they are not later reads of the buffer the body writes. Done when both shapes compile with no defk_copy_ (report copy notes and generated C), negative cases that really read the old buffer later still copy, agreement with Elixir mode incl. forced yields holds, and docs/language.md Copies mentions it. See defk-33b and defk-tif for the analysis (nested/2, taken/2, other_arms_out/2 in lib/defk/compiler.ex).

comments.text: Fixed on branch defk-8tw/loop-range-read-copy (2163954). Cause: lib/defk/compiler.ex lower_reduce/5 and reduce_while_loop/5 built loop_reads (the outer names read in the loop, which reduce_accs/7 makes live for the initial accumulator's copy test, loop_owned/2) from reads(quals) / reads(src), so st read in the first generator's range (0..(st[0] - 1)//1, also len(st) or a step) put st's buffer in 'seen' and the initial value st was copied ('the initial value of st is copied: the accumulator's buffer is the loop's alone'), once per run of the loop, i.e. once per outer iteration when nested. The init itself was never counted (it is inside the loop node, and reduce_accs reads only reads_outside), so init-only reads did not copy; the init shape copied only together with a range read. Fix: quals_reads/1 leaves out the first generator's range (start, end, step: evaluated once, before the first iteration and before any write; later iterations read the accumulator). Kept: an array the first generator walks (x <- st), later generators (evaluated again per outer value, reading the outer st) and filters. Reads of the pre-loop binding after the loop still copy (env.live). Reproduction (outer for over r, inner for k <- 1..(st[0]-1)//1, reduce: st): before 1 copy note + 1 defk_copy_i64, r=100k 6.1 ms; after none, 0.18 ms. Tests (test/value_semantics_test.exs 'defk-8tw'): range_bound (nested for), range_top, range_len, range_step, range_init (inner reduce_while with range+init reading st in a tif-style branch), init_reads: no copy note, no defk_copy_, agreement properties, forced yields. Negatives still copying and agreeing: range_old_after (alias read after), range_second_gen, range_walks, range_filter. Mutations: no fix fails the positive test; dropping every range generator fails range_second_gen (property + test), dropping the first generator even for an array walk fails range_walks, dropping filters fails range_filter. Docs: language.md Copies (array accumulator bullet), performance.md 6.24, cdcl_sat.exs notes (locals kept, kernels unchanged). mix ci passes.

title: A nested loop whose range or init reads the array it updates copies that array
